Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

skmle 0.1.0

  • Initial CRAN release.

Survival outcomes with sparse longitudinal covariates

  • skmle() fits the transformed hazards family (proportional hazards, additive hazards and the Box-Cox transformations between them) by the sieve maximum kernel-weighted log-likelihood estimator of Sun, Sun, Zhao and Cao (2025).
  • kee_cox() and kee_additive() fit the proportional and additive hazards models by kernel-weighted estimating equations.
  • skmle_cv() selects the bandwidth by subject-level cross-validation and refits on the full data.
  • sim_skmle_data() simulates sparse longitudinal survival data.
  • Half and full Epanechnikov kernels (w_epan_half(), w_epan_full()), and a weight argument that takes any function of the standardised lag.

Asynchronous longitudinal outcomes

  • kee_async() fits generalised linear models with time-invariant coefficients by the kernel-weighted estimating equations of Cao, Zeng and Fine (2015), with identity, log and logistic links and a half or full kernel.
  • kee_async_td() estimates time-dependent coefficients pointwise.
  • sim_async_data() simulates a response and a covariate on independent observation-time streams.

Shared

  • coef(), vcov(), confint(), nobs(), print(), summary() and plot() methods, and the broom generics tidy(), glance() and augment().
